entries.title: Matthew Boyd, Nico Hoerner strut their stuff in Cubs' win over Twins
entries.summary: <p>For different reasons, starting pitcher Matthew Boyd and second baseman Nico Hoerner did not have the first halves of the season they or the Cubs envisioned. Boyd dealt with injuries, and Hoerner simply underperformed</p><p>But there's still time for them to give the Cubs what they need. And as both showed Saturday, they have the ability to contribute.</p><p>"Everything is just moving in the right direction: endurance, how you feel through the outing and afterward," said Boyd, who threw six innings and allowed one run in the Cubs' 6-2 win over the Twins. "All that's feeling good."</p><p>The Cubs were counting on Boyd, an All-Star last year, to steady a rotation that was hit with the season-ending injury to Cade Horton and continuing uncertainty around Justin Steele. Instead, Boyd had been one of the numerous Cubs pitchers to spend time on the injured list, including a stint that came after a knee injury he sustained playing with his kids.</p><p>Now that he's healthy, Boyd is providing what the Cubs expected. Saturday was Boyd's third straight start of at least six innings, and he has a 2.57 ERA since coming off the IL on June 25.</p><p>And because of the time on the IL, Boyd's arm might be fresher than it would be if he had stayed in the rotation all season. Boyd has thrown just 52 innings so far; by July 22 of last year he had already tossed 118 2/3.</p><p>"There is definitely a silver lining to that," said Boyd, who reached 10 years of service time Friday. "You don't know what tomorrow's going to hold [so] you just react. That's the only thing you can do, is control your reaction."</p><p>Hoerner also kept control of his emotions after Saturday's game when he had four hits for the fifth time in his career. Signed to a six-year, $141 million contract extension in March that established him as a long-term piece of the Cubs' core, Hoerner is still playing his usual strong defense, but the bat hasn't kept up.</p><p>Even with Saturday, Hoerner's on-base percentage is at .313. He hopes his day against the Twins — when he had four singles, scored once and drove in another run — is a sign of better things to come.</p><p>"I'm going to do my best," Hoerner said. "I'm going to attack the game and prepare hard and compete. Our team's in a really great place and I know I am. I'm lucky to be healthy and to be confident and I'm excited for everything the rest of the year has in store."</p><p>Hoerner acknowledged he has not been productive or helped the Cubs score runs. His track record says he can, and Saturday he illustrated what he can bring to the lineup.</p><p>"It was coming," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. "A good time to get it."</p><p>Both Boyd and Hoerner were helped Saturday by Michael Busch, whose first-inning home run gave the Cubs a 1-0 lead. The 402-foot drive ended up in the hands of Anthony Rizzo, who was sitting in the right-field bleachers with his 2016 teammates.</p><p>As cute a moment as that was, Rizzo coming away with a home run ball won't have any impact on the rest of the year. For this group to come close to matching what the 2016 Cubs did and get the same reaction in 2036, they'll have to get contributions from players like Boyd and Hoerner.</p><p>Boyd said it would be "really fun" to experience in a decade what the 2016 team is this weekend.</p><p>"We know what we're capable of," Boyd said. "We still believe, collectively, our best baseball is ahead of us."</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Bulls' Caleb Wilson is a summer winner after dazzling in Vegas
entries.summary: <p>LAS VEGAS — There were a few down moments for Caleb Wilson in his first three Summer League games.</p><p>He missed too many free throws and had some bad turnovers.</p><p>But my, oh, my, were there highs for the Bulls rookie.</p><p>The franchise has been searching for “that dude” for years, and it might have found him with the No. 4 overall pick. And it’s not just his athleticism and two-way above-the-rim game. There’s a swagger that Wilson carries with him that few Bulls have displayed since Joakim Noah was patrolling the paint over a decade ago.</p><p>Wilson just gets it.</p><p>He does the right things and says the right things.</p><p>While top picks AJ Dybantsa and Darryn Peterson were sitting out back-to-backs — both against the Bulls coincidentally — Wilson was asking vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham to let him play.</p><p>“I wanted to win a game before I stop,” Wilson said to reporters after the Bulls’ victory over the Dybantsa-less Wizards on Tuesday night. “I don’t get to play again until October, probably, or whenever the season starts. I’m just trying to learn as much as I can, and there’s no better place to do that than Summer League.”</p><p>Asked about Peterson and Dybantsa skipping a showdown with him and the Bulls, Wilson, 19, said that he’s “different from all of them.’’</p><p>“I can’t say they don’t enjoy basketball, but I enjoy basketball,’’ he said. ‘‘I love this [expletive]. I’m going to play as much as I can, as much as my team will let me. I’m not the type to go away from a game because I don’t feel good because I know in the NBA, I’m not going to feel good some games. As long as I don’t have an injury or something that’s wrong with me, I’m gonna play every time. People come from all over the world to see me play, so I don’t want to let them down.”</p><p>Wilson need not worry about that, averaging 24.3 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.3 blocks and 1.3 steals while shooting 60% from the field and 50% from three-point range. entries.title: Chicago sees slight air quality improvement, but hazardous conditions expected to return Sunday
entries.summary: <p>After improved air quality early Saturday, wildfire smoke from Canada was expected to return to the Chicago area Saturday night and into Sunday, prompting another Air Pollution Action Day for Illinois.</p><p>Air quality reached the "moderate" category Saturday, but that's expected to worsen to "unhealthy" Sunday. An air quality alert remained in effect through Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. </p><p>“The general expectation is for a gradual deterioration in air quality through [Saturday] night,” said Jake Petr, meteorologist at the weather service.</p><p>The smoky haze is expected to linger into Monday, Petr said. Beyond that, the forecast remains uncertain because wildfire smoke will continue drifting into the region as fires burn in Canada and Minnesota. As long as those fires remain active, smoky conditions could persist.</p><p>Chicago experienced its <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/07/16/wildfire-smoke-air-quality-kn95-mask-sales" target="_blank" ><u>worst air quality Thursday</u></a>, when wildfire smoke pushed the city into the ranks of the world's most polluted major cities. The weather conditions prompted city officials to close the beaches and several events throughout the area were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/environment/2026/07/16/air-quality-outdoor-events-canceled-list-concerts-beaches" target="_blank" >canceled</a>. </p><p>Beaches and city pools reopened Friday afternoon, though the Chicago Park District said programming would be moved indoors. The Garfield Park Conservatory, Lincoln Park Conservatory and the Morton Arboretum in suburban Lisle were also open Saturday. </p><p>Petr urged residents to check the air quality before going outside and to protect themselves by wearing masks. Those with breathing issues should remain indoors.</p><p>In addition to the smoke, rain showers rolled through the Chicago area Saturday morning and early afternoon. However, rain would do little to clear the smoky conditions, Petr said.</p><p>Sunny conditions were expected Sunday, but lingering smoke is likely to remain as temperatures dip into the low 80s.</p><p><i>Kade Heather contributing.</i></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/07/16/wildfire-smoke-prompts-air-quality-alert-for-most-of-chicago-area-to" >‘Hazardous’ Canadian wildfire smoke prompts air quality warning for Chicago. entries.title: Mount Carmel linebacker Roman Igwebuike says everything about Notre Dame ‘felt right’ on official visit
entries.summary: <p>There hasn’t been much of a Catholic League-to-South Bend pipeline in recent years, but that might be changing.</p><p>Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman added his second elite recruit from the Chicago area when Mount Carmel linebacker Roman Igwebuike announced his commitment live on 247Sports’ YouTube channel last week.</p><p>Igwebuike, who had more than 50 scholarship offers, is a four-star prospect who is No. 9<br>in Illinois in the 2027 cycle, No. 10 nationally among linebackers and No. 152 in 247Sports’ composite rankings. He joins St. Patrick defensive lineman David Folorunsho, the No. 2 rising senior in the state, in the Irish’s 2027 class.</p><p>Why did Igwebuike pick Notre Dame over Clemson, Indiana, Missouri and Tennessee, which were his other finalists?</p><p>‘‘I went on three visits; my official visit was the best,’’ he said on the commitment video. ‘‘It felt right, everything about it — the program, the way they take care of their players on and off the field.’’</p><p>He also likes that Freeman played linebacker at Ohio State and has shown an ability to develop players at that position.</p><p>National recruiting analyst Clint Cosgrove sees it as a good fit for the 6-3, 220-pound<br>Igwebuike and for the Irish.</p><p>‘‘He grew into his frame,’’ Cosgrove told the Sun-Times. ‘‘Those young guys, sometimes they seem like baby giraffes when they’re growing into their frame.’’</p><p>Igwebuike had a team-best 115 tackles during the Caravan’s unbeaten run to the Class 8A title last fall. He also had 13½ tackles for loss, seven sacks, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery.</p><p>‘‘An exceptional run defender,’’ according to Cosgrove, Igwebuike also can make plays in the passing game.</p><p>‘‘[He has] the ability to play sideline to sideline [and is] very versatile,’’ Cosgrove said. ‘‘He can fit into any defense.’’</p><p>Igwebuike is the fifth Mount Carmel prospect in the 2027 cycle to make a Power Four commitment. The others are wide receiver Quentin Burrell and cornerback Tavares Harrington, both of whom picked Michigan; edge rusher Darin Graham (Wisconsin); and offensive tackle Chase Clark (Purdue).</p><p>And Igwebuike’s decision leaves only one uncommitted prospect among the top 20 in the state: Brother Rice four-star defensive lineman Brayden Parks.</p><h3>Public League update</h3><h3></h3><p>The Public League has realigned its conferences, shrinking the top-tier Red from 16 to 12 and rebranding the upper-tier White as a second Red tier.</p><p>One top Red conference will feature King, Morgan Park, Payton, Phillips, Simeon and Taft. The other will feature Amundsen, Bulls Prep, Kenwood, Lane, Lincoln Park and Young.</p><p>In a new wrinkle this year, the top Red conference winners will play in Week 9 to determine the Public League regular-season champion.</p><p>Westinghouse, Brooks, Clark and Johnson will move down from the top-tier Red to the second-tier Red.</p><p>The second-tier Red and the White each will have four six-team conferences. The rest of the teams will be in three Blue conferences.</p><h3>Caravan on ESPN</h3><p>Mount Carmel’s Week 2 home game Aug. 28 against St. Joseph Regional from Montvale, New Jersey, will be broadcast on ESPN. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. St. Joseph went 10-2 and won a private-school state title last season.<br></p>

entries.title: Connor Bedard's agent spells out Blackhawks contract negotiations, shoulder surgery decision
entries.summary: <p>Over the last six weeks, dating back to the NHL combine in early June, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks?_gl=1*w5m7kx*_up*MQ..*_ga*NzI2OTI5NzcyLjE3ODQ0MzE4MTM.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODQ0MzE4MTMkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODQ0MzE4MTMkajYwJGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> and Connor Bedard went back and forth on contract negotiations.</p><p>Bedard's agent, Don Meehan, laid out the process to the Sun-Times on Saturday, shortly after Bedard <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/18/connor-bedard-blackhawks-new-contract-nhl-free-agency" target="_blank" >signed a five-year deal</a> carrying a $15 million salary-cap hit.</p><p>"We had a long discussion about term," Meehan said. "There were many variables that we considered. A shorter-term deal would've put in Connor in absolute control — if it were, for example, a three-year deal — in terms of the current economic climate.</p><p>"But Chicago explained, from their point of view, that what was important to them was continuity and stability. [General manager Kyle Davidson] indicated they wanted to send a signal internally and externally. If Connor was there for a considerable period of time, [that would] provide the stability and continuity the organization looked for, and that was met with Connor's approval."</p><p>Meehan confirmed the Hawks initially pushed for an even longer deal, but five years was determined to be a fair compromise given how little is known about what stars' salaries will look like in 2031.</p><p>"We know the cap is changing," Meehan said. "People are suggesting there might be an 8% increase every year. Whether that's accurate or not, it leads all of us to believe the marketplace is changing dramatically. In that respect, both sides wanted to be in a position where nobody's side was being distorted one way or another.</p><p>"I know that was particularly sensitive from Connor's point of view. I think Chicago understood that, and...[they were] happy that at least we were talking a five-year deal as opposed to something less."</p><p>A month into Bedard's negotiations, Ducks forward Leo Carlsson's record-setting offer sheet — carrying an $18 million cap hit — sent tremors through the league. </p><p>And Carlsson's agent, Matt Keator, later told Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman they had been waiting for Bedard to set the market for restricted free agents before the Flyers approached. But the same wasn't true on the opposite side.</p><p>"We understood that Connor had a very great presence in Chicago, both on the ice statistically and off the ice dramatically in terms of the economic impact on the franchise," Meehan said. "We weren't waiting for anybody else."</p><p>Following the offer sheet, Bedard's camp decided not to fluctuate from the position they had already set, which meant Bedard's contract ultimately came in $3 million per year below Carlsson's.</p><p>Meehan said Bedard, who will personally speak to reporters Monday, hopes the contract sends a strong message affirming his commitment to the Hawks.</p><p>"[He] believes in the direction of the team, really believes in his teammates and doesn't accept well any kind of criticism of the organization or his teammates or anything," Meehan said.</p><h3><b>Shoulder surgery</b></h3><p>The left shoulder injury Bedard suffered while skating July 2 in Vancouver also threw a wrench into his eventful offseason. </p><p>Bedard first traveled to Chicago to get an MRI on his left shoulder from Dr. Michael Terry, the Hawks' team physician, and then traveled to Vail, Colorado, to get a second opinion from Dr. Peter Millett.</p><p>Millett determined there was "a touch more damage" to Bedard's left shoulder from this accident than there had been to his right shoulder last December, Meehan said. Millett and Terry both suggested surgery, which Bedard decided to undertake, sidelining him for an estimated four months.</p><p>"I don't think there were any regrets [about not getting surgery last year], because he came back stronger than ever and felt he wasn't being affected in any negative way," Meehan said. "But I think he was cautious in relation to Dr. Terry and Dr. Millett's suggestions. </p><p>"The fear in Connor's mind...was if he attempted to rehab and felt the shoulder was still unstable, it really would have been lost time, so to speak."</p><p>Meehan said doctors believe the two shoulder injuries in an eight-month span to be coincidental. They have "no concerns" about his ability to make a full recovery.</p><p>And the four-month recovery timeline is estimated for a reason.</p><p>"As I said to Kyle, 'You better be prepared. After three and a half months, he'll be in your office, and he's not going to be a very positive guy if you don't give him clearance to play. He'll be miserable to live with,'" Meehan said. "[Kyle] laughed and said, 'I understand that all too well. I remember the jaw [injury].'</p><p>"[Connor is] absolutely determined. He's been talking about a very aggressive form of rehab. There's no reservations about him being totally committed to...being back as soon as possible."</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Relatives go out of their way to hurt woman's feelings
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> After many years living near and helping my parents, I moved to another state to retire. My dad died three months after I moved. I begged my mother to let me fly back and help her with his arrangements, but she insisted I stay put.</p><p>Some weeks later, and two days after we had talked on the phone, she secretly buried my dad's ashes without telling me. I was devastated to receive a pathetic video of her, my brother, and a priest conducting a private service. Though she won't admit it, I think she was punishing me for moving away.</p><p>Mom is mentally ill and narcissistic, and there have been many betrayals before this one. As the eldest daughter, I appear to be her main target, and my siblings make excuses for her behavior. (My brother said, "It wasn't my job to call you.") It has been two years, but she doesn't think she did anything wrong. How do I get over this? I loved my dad so much. — <i>MISTREATED IN ARIZONA</i></p><p><b>DEAR MISTREATED:</b> Please accept my deepest sympathy for the loss of your father. A step in the right direction for getting past this would be to remind yourself that your mother is mentally ill and narcissistic. It appears from what you have told me that you have always been the scapegoat in the family, which may be why your brother didn't alert you to what your mother was planning.</p><p>Of course you loved your father. I am sure he loved you very much. If you know where his ashes are interred, it might be a comfort to visit there. However, if you don't know, I wouldn't blame you for moving on with your life and spending it with people who appreciate you for the fine person you are.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I've known my wife for 22 years. We had a lot of on and off during those years. The last time we got back together, we married. It's been almost five years now.</p><p>Recently, we had an argument that has her not wanting me to touch her. She refuses to discuss the problem. It feels like she hates me. When I asked if she wanted a divorce, she said, "I don't know." I don't want to lose her, but her actions since that argument make me think it's really over. Silence in my own house is ridiculous to me. And not even allowing me to touch her feels like she has really given up on us.</p><p>I mentioned marriage counseling, and again her response was, "I don't know." I feel like I should just go file for divorce, but that's not really what I want. Please give me some advice on what to do. — <i>BEYOND CONFUSED IN PENNSYLVANIA</i></p><p><b>DEAR BEYOND CONFUSED:</b> Tell your wife you are not willing to continue being married under the present circumstances. Then return to the subject of marriage counseling. If she is willing to go with you, ask your doctor or your health insurance company to give you a list of qualified marriage and family therapists. The two of you are at a stalemate, and without mediation, your situation won't change.</p><p><i>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren, also known as Jeanne Phillips, and was founded by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 69440, Los Angeles, CA 90069.</i></p><p>For an excellent guide to becoming a better conversationalist and a more sociable person, order "How to Be Popular." Send your name and mailing address, plus check or money order for $8 (U.S. funds), to: Dear Abby, Popularity Booklet, P.O. Box 446, Kings Mills, OH 45034-0446. (Shipping and handling are included in the price.)</p>

entries.title: One bad Apple (update) can spoil the whole week
entries.summary: <p>Apple sneaks into your living room at night and rearranges the furniture.</p><p>In the morning, you come downstairs and see the couch is not where it belongs, the chairs turned facing the wall, the hutch, askew. You go to put your everything back in place, and can't. The couch is too heavy. The chairs, somehow bolted to the floor. The knicknacks are missing.</p><p>So you call Apple. Together, virtually, you push furniture this way and that. For nearly an hour. But when you're done, the living room is somehow still not right. You could live with it this way. But why should you have to? You want it the way it was.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-c20000" name="module-c20000"></a> <div class="RichTextSidebarModule-title">Opinion bug</div> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h2>Opinion</h2></div> </div><p>Welcome to my week with Apple, a company I've been patronizing with canine devotion for nearly 25 years. I own a half dozen devices, including a spanking new iMac desktop computer, bought last January. Paid for extra memory.</p><p>So when a little notice appears that it is time for the Tahoe 26.5.1 update, I do not feel a protective frisson of fear. . These updates are necessary, for security. I click my approval and go to bed.</p><p>I awake to a changed world. My screen saver, for years a view of the Grand Canal in Venice, now replaced by some rock strewn aqua lake. The icons on my desktop are not in their familiar disarray, but assembled in neat rows, as if by some sociopath.</p><p>But that isn't the bad part. The bad part is when I open my photos, I find 1,640. Not the 88,000 possessed the day before.</p><p>No problem. Up into iCloud. There they all are. Whew. And I could leave it like that. But clouds blow away. Things happen. I paid extra for the terabyte of memory on my machine because I want the photos at hand, where I can edit them, which you can't do in the cloud. So I begin to download the photos.</p><p>Only they won't go. I get to 10,000 or so, and the thing freezes up. I try various strategies, guided first by AI, then phoning, reaching a very realistic voice. We try this, then that ,then this again. Only it doesn't work. Nothing works.</p><p>Eventually, I 'm passed along to an actual human. Very nice. We work together for another hour. No luck.</p><p>Throughout it all, I tell myself: The photos are in the cloud. Human agency will get them out. On Day Four, another human has me download a new update, 26.5.2. I wonder if it has just been issued to address the nest of bugs caused by the last update.</p><p>So I contact Apple media relations, and that is really why I'm writing this — well, that and to complain.</p><p>I wonder — is this how the system is set up? To wipe away our photos, so they have to live in the Cloud? Force us to depend on them? "It seems odd to me that this would happen automatically — taking the library off my iMac — and I am wondering if this is intentional, or a glitch? Are others complaining about it?"</p><p>I hear from someone — or something — with the musical, perhaps improbable, name, Vivi Du Pond, who keeps trying to push me toward various automatic systems, while ignoring my actual questions. "How frequently do updates cause problems such as this? How many human support staff does Apple employ? Other people said it is a good practice to wait, for the kinks to be worked out, before downloading an update. Is that a smart practice?"</p><p>"Thanks for your questions," she (or should that be "it"?) replies, "but we don't have anything further to share on this."</p><p>Eventually, our efforts bear fruit. The photos start transferring and keep transferring. Joy. I get Venice back up, on the third try. I finally understand — duh — their shot of Lake Tahoe. (Get it? Tahoe the operating system, Tahoe the lake).</p><p>What I still don't grasp is, in what world does Apple think, "Hey, let's swap our branded screensaver for whatever our users actually choose for themselves"?</p><p>Maybe in the world we're hurtling toward. Or dwelling in.</p><p>It never stops. This morning, my iPhone gave me this message.</p><p>"Software Update Tonight iOS 26.5.2 will be installed when iPhone is locked and has enough battery to update."</p><p>My choices are "Update Now" and "Cancel Update." I really want to choose the latter. But hit the former. Watching the little line as the update builds, I resist the urge to shut off the phone, stop the download. A few minutes later, it is done. The phone seems unharmed.</p><p>The future races at us, and not one necessarily crafted for our comfort, convenience or peace of mind. But cope with it we must.</p>

entries.title: Man in critical condition after Gold Coast stabbing
entries.summary: <p>A man was hospitalized in critical condition Saturday night after he was stabbed in the neck in the Gold Coast by an unknown woman.</p><p>Chicago police said Sunday morning the man was believed to be about 44 or 45 years old. </p><p>The man had approached the woman and a physical altercation followed at about 9:35 p.m. Saturday in the first block of East Oak Street, police said.</p><p>The woman produced a sharp object and struck the man before fleeing on foot in an unknown direction, according to police.</p><p>The man suffered a laceration to his neck and was taken to Northwestern Hospital in critical condition, police said.</p><p>Area Three Detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.summary: <p>A 50-year-old man was hospitalized after being shot in the left thigh Saturday afternoon in Austin, police said.</p><p>An unknown assailant inside a black SUV fired a shot in the direction of the man, who was in an alley in the 700 block of North Menard Avenue, about 3:25 p.m., police said.</p><p>The vehicle fled in an unknown direction, and the man was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in fair condition.</p><p>Area Four Detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Sean Newcomb keeps coming through in 'all the big spots' for White Sox
entries.summary: <p>TORONTO — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> reliever Sean Newcomb got himself into a bases-loaded jam shortly after entering the game Saturday and got himself out of it just as quickly. Then he pitched a clean seventh inning to keep his team in a tight contest that ended in a 1-0 loss to the Blue Jays.</p><p>It was just the latest high-leverage lockdown from the veteran lefty, who put himself <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/05/16/versatile-sean-newcomb-a-valuable-piece-of-white-sox-bullpen" >in the All-Star conversation</a> with a sparkling first half anchoring the Sox’ bullpen in a variety of roles.</p><p>“All the big spots we put him in, he continues to come through,” manager Will Venable said. “He's just so competitive, he's got good stuff. He's a big lefty with good stuff, and he likes to be out there, so we’re excited about what he's been doing."</p><p>Newcomb has covered 55 innings across 36 games, racking up 53 strikeouts and three saves, and rejuvenating his career.</p><p>“It's been a few years since I've been on a team that's been sitting in or near first place, so I’ve been having a lot more fun playing right now than I have in a while,” Newcomb said, pointing to a tightknit bullpen.</p><p>“We’ve got a little bit of everything,” he said. “Veteran pitching, you’ve got younger pitching, a group of starters who are settling in, then Grant [Taylor] in the bullpen and some of the younger relievers — Chris Murphy's settling in and showing his nasty stuff. There’s a lot to love.”</p><h3><b>Roch solid</b></h3><p>Right fielder Braden Montgomery said he was impressed by No. 1 draft pick Roch Cholowsky, whose pre-draft visit to the Sox happened to fall on the night of Montgomery’s seemingly Hollywood-written MLB debut that ended with the rookie’s 10th-inning, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/06/10/braden-montgomery-white-sox-walk-off-home-run-steve-stone-bob-costas-will-venable-colson-montgomery" target="_blank" ><u>walk-off home run</u></a>.</p><p>Not a bad way to sell the Sox to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/11/sox-get-their-man-picking-roch-cholowsky-with-top-overall-pick-in-mlb-draft" target="_blank" ><u>Cholowsky</u></a>, who got to enjoy the clubhouse celebration.</p><p>“He just seemed like a professional to me,” said Montgomery, who had a triple and a double over the weekend in Toronto. “The biggest part of all of this is the mental, the brain, the head on your shoulders, and he seemed like a professional ballplayer. entries.title: Sizzling Sean Burke, durable Davis Martin carry White Sox rotation into the second half
entries.summary: <p>TORONTO — Sean Burke had it all working on an immaculate Sunday afternoon north of the border, surrendering just two hits in the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a>’ 3-0 victory over the Blue Jays.</p><p>The tall right-hander carried over his strong month before the All-Star break with 6 ⅔ efficient innings and five strikeouts to help the Sox start the second half with a series win on the road, where an up-and-coming squad has struggled in their surprising run to contention. The Guardians' loss put the Sox a game ahead in the American League Central.</p><p>Burke's latest impressive effort came on the heels of Saturday's tough-luck loss for Davis Martin, who suddenly has a new challenger for the title of staff ace. </p><p>"We have a little friendly competition going back and forth with each other, but obviously, too, we help each other out," said Burke, whose sixth-inning walk was the first free pass he'd given up in 19 1/3 innings. </p><p>"[We're] both right-handed, probably going to see similar lineups each time out the same team," Burke said, crediting Martin for the scouting report. "Just going over what he thought worked and what he thinks I can get away with... Being able to bounce ideas off him is good."</p><p>The Jays didn't get a hit off Burke until the fourth inning, one of two weak singles they mustered. The Sox couldn’t find any offense either against Trey Yesavage until Colson Montgomery scratched out an infield single in the top of the fourth inning after a walk to Miguel Vargas, who came home on Andrew Benintendi’s sacrifice fly.</p><p>Montgomery later smacked his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/07/03/before-first-anniversary-of-white-sox-debut-colson-montgomery-recalls-his-first-big-moment" target="_blank" ><u>team-leading</u></a> 24th home run of the season, and the Sox got an RBI single from Braden Montgomery, who made a sliding catch in the ninth inning with the Jays threatening, helping Grant Taylor lock down his fifth save.</p><p>"Sean, the way he's been pitching, we know we're going to get his best every single day," Colson Montgomery said. "He's a dog... I just think he's elevated his game for sure."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Colson Montgomery goes deep! <a href="https://t.co/rEuUrBtC7V">pic.twitter.com/rEuUrBtC7V</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://x.com/whitesox/status/2078896606393295089?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">July 19, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Burke’s effort marked his sixth straight solid outing since mid-June, which manager Will Venable attributed to “just being aggressive with the fastball."</p><p>“You can feel it when he's doing it,” Venable said. “His confidence in it just kind of radiates from him... entries.title: Matt Shaw knows he's in trade rumors; he just doesn't want to hear about it
entries.summary: <p>Cubs utilityman Matt Shaw knows his name is churning through the rumor mill, with the trade deadline almost two weeks away. He just doesn’t want to hear about it.</p><p>Sometimes, though, it’s out of his control.</p><p>“The only time I’ll know if I’m in trade talk is when a family member says, ‘Hey, I read this,’ and I’m like, ‘Oh, I didn’t know that,’ ” Shaw told the Sun-Times on Sunday.</p><p>Indeed, while Shaw recovers from a sprained left hand, his name is all over the place as possible trade bait for the pitching-hungry Cubs. Having shown his versatility — he has played everywhere but pitcher, catcher and shortstop this season — the 2023 first-round draft pick might help the Cubs net some quality pitching.</p><p>But he learned during his rookie season, when he was yearning to know whether he’d made the big-league roster for the Japan Series, that it’s best for his well-being to stay in the dark.</p><p>“I was reading every news article about the team because I didn’t know anything,” Shaw said. “So I got really caught up in that, and it was super stressful. It was in my mind all the time. But I learned from that experience I can’t watch any of that stuff. And that was a really helpful lesson. Now I don’t read anything, I don’t look at anything.”</p><p>Shaw’s focus is on healing from the injury he suffered fouling off a pitch June 28. He said it’s still sore, and teammates who’ve had hand/wrist issues have told him they can take a long time to heal. Shaw grew impatient with the injury and wanted to tough it out, but he realized it was best to take a step back and let it heal.</p><p>The Cubs are trying everything to expedite his recovery.</p><p>“The technology in the training room is unbelievable,” Shaw said. “I don’t know what it’s all doing, but we’re doing four, five different things every single day. Ice and heat, we have a red-light lazer, some sort of electricity.”</p><p>Shaw said he has been able to stay in shape by throwing, sprinting and working out. The one thing he can’t do is hit. But that hasn’t been a problem for him this season. His slash numbers are all up from his rookie season, and his OPS+ is 105 — 136 against left-handers. Shaw said he doesn’t know when he’ll be able to hit again.</p><p>“It was one of those things where I just assumed that by now it would be healed and I’d be building up,” he said. “But that’s kind of the thing about assuming things. You set expectations, you don’t really know how the body is going to respond. I’ve never had an injury like this before.”</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Chicagoans turn out to watch Argentina vs. Spain in World Cup final
entries.summary: <p>As soon as Lauren Boyer heard there was going to be a free World Cup final watch party in Pilsen, she knew she had to be there. And all of her friends did too.</p><p>They were among dozens of soccer fans gathered at Harrison Park Sunday afternoon to watch the game, cheering and covering their mouths during tense moments. Some even raised their own red and yellow cards — paint samples from a nearby chain hardware store — the few times the stream cut out or when they disagreed with officials.</p><p>While the game ended in tears for Boyer, who was donning a Lionel Messi jersey — Spain defeated Argentina, expanding its undefeated streak to 38 and continuing an unchallenged run that has been ongoing since early 2024 — there was some joy. She was happy she got to watch the game along with her neighbors and kick a ball around with strangers even if it meant seeing one of the sport’s biggest legends end his career on a loss.</p><p>“Soccer is a lot about community and coming together,” Boyer said. “I don’t think we got enough of it during the cup.”</p><p>“And you get to meet your neighbors,” said Christopher King, Boyer’s friend and a 33-year-old Beverly resident.</p><p>Spain’s World Cup win is its first since 2010 — the last time they faced longtime teammate Messi.</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: Shota Imanaga looks like his dominant self again in Cubs' rout of Twins
entries.summary: <p>If Shota Imanaga keeps pitching this way, maybe the Cubs’ rotation won’t be in such bad shape.</p><p>Maybe. He’s still just one-fifth of the equation.</p><p>But that one-fifth gave the Cubs more than enough Sunday, throwing seven scoreless innings in a 10-1 walloping of the Twins at Wrigley Field.</p><p>“[He was] just on the attack, lots of strikes,” manager Craig Counsell said of Imanaga, who threw 63 of his 99 pitches for strikes. “Split-finger was excellent. Anytime you get seven innings from your starter, you’re in good shape.”</p><p>And anytime that starter gets 10 runs of support, you’re in better shape. Nico Hoerner had a bases-loaded triple and an RBI single. Michael Busch went 3-for-5 with an RBI, and Alex Bregman hit a two-out, two-run homer in the first.</p><p>But the day belonged to Imanaga, who’s moving further away from a brutal four-game stretch in which he had a 10.80 ERA, raising his season number from 2.32 to 4.74. His performance Sunday lowered it to 3.91. Counsell said the biggest difference has been limiting the damage.</p><p>“Shota is going to give up home runs,” Counsell said. “That’s the nature of his arsenal. But when they come and how they come has to be a part of it. He is limiting the home run right now. The walk limitation I’m also a big fan of. He’s done a really good job of that.”</p><p>Imanaga walked one batter, in the fourth inning, and he was eliminated in the next at-bat on an around-the-horn double play. It was one of several fine defensive plays by the Cubs that included a long-running catch by center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong that ended with him crashing into the wall. Never mind that the score was 10-0 at the time.</p><p>“That pitch was a mistake pitch on me,” Imanaga said through a translator. “[Catcher Carson Kelly] wanted a different spot to set up a different pitch. I felt like I threw it in the zone where the hitter could hit it.</p><p>“It’s really helpful when you know that any bullets hit to him, there’s a possibility that he’s going to make the catch. Knowing that he’s behind you allows you to attack the zone more. He’s been saving a lot of runs for us.”</p><p>But Imanaga made few mistakes, becoming the only Cubs starter this season with two starts of at least seven scoreless innings. The other came May 2 against the Diamondbacks. In seven starts since that four-game skid, Imanaga has allowed more than two runs once.</p><p>“He’s been good,” Bregman said. “I thought he executed all five pitches really well today. That’s huge when he’s got his five-pitch mix working. The splits were good, the spin was good. Heaters were good up. A few sinkers, too.”</p><p>With Jameson Taillon expected to come off the injured list Monday and Matthew Boyd throwing well again, the Cubs just might have three-fifths of a strong rotation. Though Colin Rea has been pitching better of late, the Cubs could find an upgrade. And David Peterson could very well be a placeholder for a potential acquisition. The rotation is by no means in tip-top shape.</p><p>But Imanaga appears to be reasserting himself as the staff ace he was in 2024, when he went 15-3 with a 2.91 ERA and finished fifth in Cy Young voting. For someone who seemingly was headed elsewhere in the offseason — when the Cubs declined their option on Imanaga’s contract and he declined his option, becoming a free agent before accepting the Cubs’ one-year qualifying offer — this reunification just might work out.</p><p>“With the pitching coaches giving me feedback and data about what I’ve done well, what I’ve done poorly, and trying to make the good points better, as well as working on what I need to work on, I felt like I was able to accomplish that,” Imanaga said of his return to form. “I feel like I’m not a complete pitcher yet; I’m not the final product. But I’m confident I can get better there.”</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: Air quality alert for Chicago extended through Monday as wildfire smoke from Canada lingers
entries.summary: <p>The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency has extended the Areawide Air Pollution Action Day through Monday as wildfire smoke from Canada continues to affect air quality throughout Illinois.</p><p>An EPA alert said particulate pollution is forecast to reach or exceed the “Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups” category in all or nearly all Illinois Air Quality Index forecast sectors Monday.</p><p>“For the rest of today and into tomorrow areas both inside and outside of the Action Day coverage area may experience smoke to a varying degree and duration,” said Kim Biggs, public information officer with Illinois EPA.</p><p>Residents should check the <a class="Link" href="https://www.airnow.gov/" target="_blank" >NowCast AQI </a>to monitor air quality conditions to identify periods of poor and cleaner air quality throughout the day regardless of the level of the daily forecasted Air Quality Index, Biggs said, adding, “This will also be a helpful tip on Monday anywhere in Illinois as smoke levels are likely to significantly decrease over Illinois progressively from southwest to northeast from around midday through the evening hours."</p><p>An air quality alert remains in effect through Monday, the National Weather Service said Sunday.</p><p>Meteorologist Gino Izzi said visibility has improved considerably since Thursday, when Chicago experienced its <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/07/16/wildfire-smoke-air-quality-kn95-mask-sales" target="_blank" ><u>worst air quality</u></a>, and Friday morning, when smoke was much thicker near the surface.</p><p>“Meteorologically, the visibility is what’s most impacted by the smoke,” Izzi said. “The thickness of the smoke near the surface is much less today than it was early last week,” he said.</p><p>Izzi said stronger southwest winds are expected to develop Monday afternoon and should push any remaining smoke north and east of the Chicago area.</p><p>“If there is smoke, it should likely decrease during the afternoon,” Izzi said about Monday’s outlook.</p><p>Conditions later in the week are less certain.</p><p>Izzi said smoke could potentially return to Chicago on Tuesday night into Wednesday if there are still wildfires burning to the north and a reservoir of smoke remains, though he emphasized that forecast remains highly uncertain.</p><p>“Trying to predict how much fire and how much smoke there’s going to be four or five days out is pretty hard to do,” Izzi said.</p><p>Cooler and less humid conditions are expected by the end of the week, according to the weather service.</p><p>Despite the lingering smoke, many attractions in the city and nearby suburbs were operating normally Sunday, while some made adjustments and continued to monitor air quality conditions.</p><p>The Chicago Park District listed beaches as open Sunday on its website but displayed a banner at the top of the <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagoparkdistrict.com/facilities/beaches" target="_blank" >page</a> alerting the public that the Illinois EPA had declared an Air Pollution Action Day for the Chicago metro area and that Air Quality Index levels were in the orange category, which may be unhealthy for sensitive groups.</p><p>Six Flags Great America and Hurricane Harbor in north suburban Gurnee were operating as usual Sunday.</p><p>The Morton Arboretum in west suburban Lisle remained open but canceled outdoor volunteer activities while continuing to monitor air quality conditions, spokesperson Ellyn Fortino said.</p><p>Chicago Architecture Center river cruises were also operating as usual. Spokesman Rob Walton said patrons aboard First Lady boats have access to air-conditioned cabins with filtered air.</p><p>At the Chicago Botanic Garden in north suburban Glencoe, classes scheduled onsite Sunday were held indoors, while tours and other outdoor offerings continued as usual, spokesperson Erin Benassi said.</p><p><b></b> Navy Pier said Sunday afternoon that regular programming would proceed as planned but that it would continue to assess conditions throughout the day.</p><p>“Navy Pier is continuing to monitor the air quality to ensure the safety and comfort of our guests and dedicated staff,” the pier said in an emailed statement. <b></b></p><p>Air quality can affect both visitors and animals at the Lincoln Park Zoo, though the zoo remained open on Sunday.</p><p>Depending on air quality conditions, spokesperson Anna Cieslik said care teams evaluate whether any animals might experience respiratory issues or otherwise be affected by the smoke.</p><p>Animals with outdoor habitats always have access to indoor spaces, and some have chosen to go inside during the recent smoke, she said.</p><p>Care teams also adjust animals’ enrichment and feeding strategies to avoid strenuous activity during air quality alerts.</p><p>“No animal is being strictly kept inside right now. That’s a call we only like to make in the most extreme situations because it can have an outweighed negative impact on their welfare,” Cieslik said. “But with the air quality we’ve been having lately, some animals are going inside on their own.”</p><p>Smoke also affected events around the Chicago area over the weekend.</p><p>When Paul Simon came to the stage Saturday night at Ravinia in Highland Park, the singer told the audience he was changing the order of his set because the air quality was getting worse and he was going to perform older songs first in case people needed to leave.</p><p>Ravinia said Sunday afternoon that performances by the Steans Institute and the Chicago Symphony Orchestra would proceed as scheduled, while encouraging guests to monitor air quality reports and determine their own comfort level with attending.</p><p><i>Contributing: Lynn Sweet</i></p>
